10 Best Motorcycle Cafes in the UK

Every great ride deserves a great stop. These 10 cafes are pilgrimage sites for British bikers. Read our Best Motorcycle Roads in Scotland: 15 Must-Ride Routes guide for more. Read our UK Motorcycle Touring Calendar guide for more. Read our Top 15 UK Motorcycle Roads Ranked guide for more. Read our NC500: Scotland's Ultimate Motorcycle Route Map guide for more. Read our The Ultimate Motorcycle Touring Packing List guide for more. Read our UK Road Hazards Every Biker Must Know guide for more.

  1. Ace Cafe London — Stonebridge. The original since 1938.
  2. Squires Cafe — Sherburn-in-Elmet, Yorkshire. Weekend mecca.
  3. Box Hill Cafe — Surrey Hills. Sunday morning ritual.
  4. Ponderosa Cafe — Horseshoe Pass, North Wales. Mountain views.
  5. Hartside Cafe — Pennines, Cumbria. England's highest cafe.
  6. Loomies Cafe — West Meon, Hampshire. Southern favourite.
  7. Devil's Bridge Cafe — Kirkby Lonsdale, Cumbria. Dales classic.
  8. Ryka's Cafe — Box Hill, Surrey. Ducati heaven.
  9. Cafe 1000 — Peak District. Cat and Fiddle essential stop.
  10. Applecross Inn — Scotland. Reward after the Bealach na Ba.
keyTakeaways: The Ace Cafe London is the original biker cafe, open since 1938.
Squires Cafe in Yorkshire is a legendary weekend meeting point for northern riders.
The Ponderosa on the Horseshoe Pass and Hartside in the Pennines pair great food with mountain views.
Box Hill in Surrey is a long-standing Sunday morning ritual for southern bikers.
The Applecross Inn is the classic reward stop after riding the Bealach na Ba.

faq.q: What is the most famous biker cafe in the UK?
faq.a: The Ace Cafe London in Stonebridge is the most iconic. Open since 1938, it became the heart of the cafe racer scene in the 1950s and 60s and remains a pilgrimage site for bikers worldwide. It hosts regular themed nights and events, making it as much a cultural landmark as a place to eat.

faq.q: Where is England's highest biker cafe?
faq.a: Hartside Cafe sits high in the Pennines in Cumbria, reached by the rewarding A686 climb, and is renowned as England's highest cafe. The road up is a favourite among riders, and the views from the top on a clear day are superb. It is a classic stop on any northern touring route.

faq.q: Are these cafes open all year round?
faq.a: Many biker cafes are busiest and most reliably open in spring and summer, and some remote ones reduce hours or close in winter. Weekends, especially Sunday mornings in good weather, are peak times. It is always worth checking opening hours before making a long ride, particularly for the more isolated mountain and coastal cafes.

faq.q: Which biker cafe is best after riding a mountain pass?
faq.a: The Applecross Inn in Scotland is the classic reward after conquering the Bealach na Ba, while the Ponderosa on the Horseshoe Pass in North Wales offers food and mountain views after a scenic climb. Both give you a well-earned stop with fellow riders who have just tackled the same road.

faq.q: Why are biker cafes so popular with motorcyclists?
faq.a: Biker cafes combine a good stop for food and fuel with a social scene where riders swap route advice and admire each others' bikes. Many sit at the end of great riding roads, making them natural destinations. The culture dates back to the cafe racer era, giving places like the Ace Cafe genuine heritage.
